transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Lena, Ravi (Redwood) / Samir, Ava, Marcus (MercuryPay)

Summary: quick weekly POC sync focused on surge readiness, odd latency spikes during burst tests, and tuning the Dedicated pool autoscaling/burst policy. Decided on a replay stress test, a short config change to KV caching, and follow-up pricing readout.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we blocked an hour for the poc surge readiness and some of the quirks you flagged last week. um quick roll call?
[00:12] Samir: Samir here, Ava, Marcus on my side. thanks Lena.
[00:16] Ava: Ava here. seeing the increased p95 on the last run so want to figure out guardrails.
[00:22] Marcus: Marcus, CTO, quick high level: we need predictable tail latency during BlackFriday-like surges, cost is secondary but still important.
[00:32] Ravi: cool, thanks. quick agenda — 1) review the last week's burst run numbers, 2) look at autoscale policy tweaks, 3) KV/prefix cache tuning, 4) next steps + pricing impacts.

[02:05] Samir: so the spike we saw — the 1800 concurrent replay — p99 jumped to 1.4s from baseline 0.45. is that a model thing or infra?
[02:18] Ravi: yeah we dug in, there are two things. first, we saw queuing behaviour on the dedicated pool during the ramp — requests were piling up for about 12 seconds then the runtime spun up extra workers which triggered cache cold misses. second, a handful of calls hit the longer context path which forces KV rehydrates — K V cash was spelled weird in the logs — so those requests pay the cold cost.
[02:40] Ava:-k yes, that matches our logs, we also saw occasional GC spikes on our side when replay clients created many connections.

[04:00] Lena: for dedicated sizing, we recommended an initial reserved pool of 8 units for your baseline traffic, with a burst ceiling of +4 units and a hard cap at +6 for emergency. we proposed autoscale policy: target_utilization=60%, cooldown=45s, max_scale_step=2.
[04:22] Samir: interesting — can you explain the target 60% rationale?
[04:25] Ravi: sure — we've found at 60% you get headroom for short bursts without constant scale churn; at higher targets scale decisions fire too frequently and that causes worker churn and more cache misses. also it keeps queue depth low so tail latency is better.

[06:12] Marcus: but that means higher steady cost, right? how big is the delta vs target_utilization=75%?
[06:20] Lena: ballpark: running your baseline with 8 units at 60% vs 75% increases reserved unit needs roughly 18-22% — I'll send exact numbers. but it's a tradeoff: higher utilization reduces cost but increases risk of p99 regressions during spike.

[07:05] Ava: can we have burst credits or buffer that isn't billed the same as reserved?
[07:10] Lena: yes we offer a burst buffer concept — short-lived spare capacity that is billed at a higher unit rate but only when consumed. for your profile, we suggested +4 burst units with an overflow price that's about 1.7x the reserved unit rate.

[08:30] Samir: about fallback — if Dedicated hits the hard-cap should we fallback to hosted or a smaller model?
[08:36] Ravi: we can chain fallback policies: 1) fallback to cheaper model variant (quantized or smaller), 2) cross-region fallback to another Dedicated pool, 3) last-resort route to Redwood Hosted API. each has implications: model switch may change output quality, cross-region adds ~30-80ms, hosted adds cost and potential data residency concerns.
[09:00] Marcus: we prefer to avoid hosted for sensitive flows. cross-region is acceptable for low-sensitivity tasks.

[10:05] Ava: one weird thing — around minute 18 of last run we saw isolated 3-4s tails for a small percentage of requests. logs show those requests had longer prompt lengths and triggered kv rehydration. can KV cache be warmed?
[10:20] Ravi: yes, prefix/KV warmup is our recommended mitigation. two quick options: 1) seed the KV cache with expected prefixes before traffic spike (we can provide a script), 2) extend cache TTL for those keys during known surge windows. both reduce cold-miss penalty.
[11:00] Samir: can you share the script today?
[11:04] Ravi: yes I'll upload to the shared folder — link: https://redwood.app/s/hub/mercurypay/poc-kv-warmup-script — note link is internal.

[12:10] Lena: also a small note about quantization — we can run a 4bit quantized variant (gguf-ish) which reduces memory and increases throughput but quality delta is modest for your use-case. we should validate on your test prompts.
[12:34] Marcus: quality matters for fraud detection flows, so we want to A/B sample only; not a full swap.

[14:05] Samir: on autoscale cooldown — 45s seems short to me; wouldn't that cause frequent up/down during noisy load?
[14:16] Ravi: we picked 45s because your burst pattern is a rapid spike for ~90-120s then decay. cooldown prevents flip-flop; with target 60% it shouldn't bounce frequently. if you have noisy oscillation, we can increase cooldown to 120s and increase max_scale_step to 3 to move faster on big ramps.

[16:20] Ava: any observability hooks we should add? we saw some metrics gaps last week.
[16:26] Lena: yes we suggest enabling token-level latency traces and per-request routing tags, then we can correlate p99 to specific model variants or specific nodes. we'll add those tracing hooks to your console workspace.

[18:05] Samir: pricing-wise, can you sketch the delta for reserved 8 units + burst + quantized fallback?
[18:13] Lena: yes rough: reserved units base monthly commit X, burst usage billed at 1.7x of base, quantized fallback compute savings ~25% on per-token compute. I'll send a spreadsheet with three scenarios after this call.

[20:00] Marcus: can we also run a replay that mirrors our BlackFriday-peak? we've got the traces but need Redwood to run the replay against the Dedicated cluster.
[20:10] Ravi: we can run a replay. propose a 2-hour run for high fidelity plus one 30-minute warm-up. we'll capture p50/p95/p99, queue depth, and cold miss counts. target week of Jan 12.

[22:45] Samir: is there any network config for Private that changes behavior? we are evaluating Private/VPC option for sensitive flows.
[22:55] Ravi: Private deploys have customer-controlled VPC and KMS/HSM for keys; network egress and cross-region routing could add ~15-40ms. functionally same runtime but operator access paths differ; we'll provide a checklist for your security team.

[25:00] Ava: we need SOC2 and ISO docs for procurement — Marcus will kick that off.
[25:05] Marcus: yes procurement will want the SOC2 package and audit logs retention options.

[27:10] Lena: I'll attach SOC2 cert and a summary of available log retention options after the call.

[28:40] Ravi: quick note on code-level best practice — prefer connection pooling on the client side, avoid spinning up new connections per request, that aggravated GC on Ava's replay client. also prefer streaming responses if you can, reduces memory pressure.

[30:00] Samir: okay actionable items — we will provide traces and confirm which endpoints are sensitive (no-hosted).

[31:30] Lena: proposal for the immediate config change: 1) set target_utilization=60, cooldown=45s, max_scale_step=2, 2) enable 4-unit burst buffer priced at 1.7x, 3) seed KV cache before run and extend TTL to 10min for surge windows, 4) run replay on Jan 12. sound good?
[31:52] Marcus: yes with one change — increase max_scale_step to 3 to handle steeper ramps.
[32:00] Ravi: sounds reasonable. we'll simulate with both step=2 and 3 in the replay and compare.

[34:45] Ava: any quick FYIs on model variant naming? some of the telemetry used "redwood-dense-7b-v1" in logs but our dashboard shows weird spelling "redwood-dens 7 b".
[34:55] Ravi: that's the transcription/labeling mismatch; we have a mapping doc in the console, we'll add aliasing so your logs map consistently.

[37:10] Samir: last question — what's the expected lead time to add more reserved units if we decide to increase?
[37:18] Lena: for Dedicated, changes typically take under 24 hours but depends on capacity commitments. if you need guaranteed ramp we can do an on-call staffed resize with 4-6 hour lead time for urgent adds.

[40:00] Marcus: ok, good. let's schedule the Jan 14 readout. put it on calendar.
[40:07] Lena: will do. I'll send the calendar invite and the spreadsheet.

[41:30] Ravi: I'll upload the KV warmup script and the perf harness to the shared folder. link: https://redwood.app/s/hub/mercurypay/poc-perf-harness-jan07.csv

[43:00] Ava: thanks all. 
[43:05] Samir: thanks.
[43:06] Marcus: thanks.
[43:10] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and a replay schedule.

Notes & artifacts referenced: "poc-burst-run-2026-01-05.csv" (shared), autoscale_policy_examples.md, KV-warmup-script.sh, SOC2-summary.pdf (will be attached after call).

End of transcript.
